gp.heading: Gross Profit (Loss)
gp.text:
Gross profit for the quarter ended June 30, 2025, increased $2,853,000 over the same period in 2024, as follows:

Treatment Segment gross profit increased by $2,763,000 or approximately 230.8% and gross margin increased to 13.7% % from (14.3)% primarily due to higher revenue from higher waste volume and higher averaged price from waste mix. The increase in fixed costs within the Treatment Segment negatively impacted gross profit and gross margin. Services Segment gross profit increased by $90,000 or approximately 82.6% and gross margin improved slightly from (1.9)% to (0.6)%. The increases were attributed primarily to overall improved margin on projects and lower fixed costs which were offset by the impact of lower revenue. Our Services Segment gross margin is impacted by our current projects which are competitively bid on and will therefore, have varying margin structures.

Gross profit for the six months ended June 30, 2025, increased $4,130,000 over 2024, as follows:

Treatment Segment gross profit increased by $3,065,000 or approximately 245.4% and gross margin increased to 8.8% % from (7.3)% primarily due to higher revenue from higher waste volume and higher averaged price from waste mix. The increase in fixed costs within the Treatment Segment negatively impacted gross profit and gross margin.

cor.heading: Cost of Goods Sold
cor.text:
Cost of goods sold decreased $2,253,000 for the quarter ended June 30, 2025, as compared to the quarter ended June 30, 2024, as follows:

Cost of goods sold for the Treatment Segment increased by approximately $291,000 or 3.1%. Treatment Segment’s overall fixed costs were higher by approximately $682,000 resulting from the following: salaries and payroll related expenses were higher by approximately $665,000 due to additional headcount; maintenance expenses were higher by approximately $38,000; depreciation expenses were higher by $25,000; travel expense were higher by $21,000; general expenses were higher by $11,000; and regulatory expenses were lower by $78,000. Treatment Segment’s variable costs decreased by approximately $391,000 primarily due to lower disposal costs of $758,000 and lower outside services costs of $86,000, offset by overall higher material and supplies, transportation and other costs of approximately $453,000. Within our Treatment Segment, variable cost categories can fluctuate based on waste mix. Services Segment cost of goods sold decreased $2,544,000 or 44.2% primarily due to lower revenue.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
We had income tax expense of $0 and income tax benefit of $1,161,000 for continuing operations for the three months ended June 30, 2025, and the corresponding period of 2024, respectively, and income tax expense of $0 and income tax benefit of $2,117,000 for continuing operations for the six months ended June 30, 2025, and the corresponding period of 2024, respectively. Our effective tax rates were approximately 0% and 23.5% for the three months ended June 30, 2025, and the corresponding period of 2024, respectively, and 0% and 22.6% for the six months ended June 30, 2025, and the corresponding period of 2024, respectively. Our effective tax rates for the three and six months ended June 30, 2025, were impacted by our recognition of a full valuation allowance against our U.S federal and state deferred tax assets in the quarter ended September 30, 2024. Our effective tax rates for the three and six months ended June 30, 2024, were impacted by non-deductible expenses and state taxes.

On July 4, 2025, the United States enacted tax reform legislation through the “One Big Beautiful Bill Act,” which changes existing U.S. tax laws, including extending or making permanent certain provisions of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, repealing certain clean energy initiatives, in addition to other changes.

capex.heading: Capital Expenditures
capex.text: We anticipate making capital expenditures of approximately up to $6,000,000 for the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, to maintain operations and regulatory compliance requirements and support revenue growth. Our anticipated capital expenditures for 2025 include certain strategic project initiatives which include the installation of our second generation unit for our PFAS technology (see “Known Trends and Uncertainties – New Processing Technology”). We plan to fund our capital expenditures for 2025 from cash from operations, Liquidity and/or financing. The initiation and timing of our capital expenditures in 2025 are subject to a number of factors which include, among other things, cost/benefit analysis, the pace of our strategic project initiatives and improvement in our operations.

net sales.heading: Revenues
net sales.text:
Consolidated revenues increased $600,000 for the three months ended June 30, 2025, compared to the three months ended June 30, 2024, as follows:

(1) Includes wastes generated by government clients of $567,000 and $608,000 for the three months ended June 30, 2025, and the corresponding period of 2024, respectively.

Treatment Segment overall revenue increased by $3,054,000 or 36.6% for the three months ended June 30, 2025, over the same period in 2024. The overall increase in revenue in the Treatment Segment was primarily due to higher waste volume and higher averaged price waste from waste mix. Our Treatment Segment revenue was also positively impacted by our international initiatives, which resulted in an increase in revenue of approximately $558,000 or 150.8% in revenue as compared to the same period of last year. Services Segment revenue decreased by approximately $2,454,000 or 43.5%. The decrease in revenue in the Services Segment was due to reasons as discussed in the “Overview” section.

Treatment.text: Our Treatment and Services Segments’ business continues to be heavily dependent on services that we provide to federal governmental clients, primarily as subcontractors for others who are contractors to government entities or directly as the prime contractor. We believe demand for our services will continue to be subject to fluctuations due to a variety of factors beyond our control, including, without limitation, current economic and political conditions, government reductions, COVID like events, government budget issues and the manner in which the applicable government authority will be required to spend funding to remediate various sites. In addition, our governmental contracts and subcontracts relating to activities at federal governmental sites are generally subject to termination for convenience at any time, at the government’s option. Significant reductions in the level of governmental funding or specifically mandated levels for different programs that are important to our business could have a material adverse impact on our business, financial position, results of operations, and cash flows.

gp.heading: Gross Profit (Loss)
gp.text:
Gross profit for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, decreased $2,005,000 over the same period of 2025, as follows:

Treatment Segment incurred a gross loss of $225,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared with a gross profit of $2,266,000 for the same period in 2025. Gross margin declined to (1.9%) from 17.3%. The decline in gross profit and gross margin was primarily due to lower revenue resulting from reduced waste volumes and higher fixed operating costs, which were spread over a lower revenue base, further adversely impacting gross margin.

Services Segment gross profit increased by approximately $486,000, and gross margin improved to 12.2% from 6.7% in the prior-year period, primarily due to higher revenue and a more favorable mix of projects performed. Gross margins within our Services Segment are influenced by the type, scope, and mix of projects performed, which are generally competitively bid and have varying margin structures. As a result, gross margins may fluctuate from period to period based on the timing and mix of projects completed.

Gross profit for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, decreased $9,594,000 over the same period in 2025, as follows:

The Treatment Segment incurred a gross loss of $5,711,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared with a gross profit of $4,082,000 for the same period in 2025.

cor.heading: Cost of Goods Sold
cor.text:
Cost of goods sold increased $2,499,000 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, as compared to the quarter ended September 30, 2025, as follows:

Cost of goods sold for the Treatment Segment increased by approximately $978,000, or 9.0%. Treatment Segment fixed costs increased by approximately $1,094,000. Fixed salaries and payroll-related expenses increased by approximately $756,000, primarily due to increased headcount. Maintenance costs increased by approximately $196,000 due to scheduled equipment maintenance and facility security enhancements. Depreciation expense increased by approximately $66,000 due to additional capitalized equipment, including our prototype PFAS reactor. Regulatory expenses increased by approximately $49,000 due to increased regulatory activities and higher fees assessed by regulatory agencies. The remaining increases were from higher travel and general expenses totaling approximately $27,000. Treatment Segment variable costs decreased by approximately $116,000, primarily due to lower materials and supplies, transportation, and outside services costs totaling approximately $312,000, partially offset by higher disposal costs of approximately $29,000 and higher overtime expenses of approximately $167,000.

da_op.text: Cash used in operating activities from continuing operations during the first nine months of 2026 primarily reflected our net loss from continuing operations of approximately $17,046,000, adjusted for non-cash items, including stock-based compensation expense of approximately $631,000 and depreciation and amortization expense of approximately $1,469,000. Changes in operating assets and liabilities provided approximately $3,993,000 of cash, primarily reflecting a decrease in accounts receivable (net of provision for credit losses) of approximately $1,204,000, a net decrease in prepaid expenses, inventories and other assets of approximately $246,000, and a net increase in accounts payable, accrued expenses, deferred revenue, and other accrued liabilities of approximately $5,660,000. These favorable changes were partially offset by an increase in unbilled receivables of approximately $3,117,000. Accounts receivable balances are affected by the timing of customer invoicing and collections, while cash receipts are influenced by the payment terms and conditions of our customer contracts.

prov.text: Services Segment SG&A expenses decreased primarily due to a decrease in provision for credit losses of approximately $283,000 resulting from the settlement of a receivable previously determined to be uncollectible. The remaining decrease was primarily attributable to lower travel expenses of approximately $30,000 and reduced salaries and payroll-related expenses due to fewer employee hours devoted to marketing activities.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense
nonop.text: Interest expense decreased by approximately $36,000 and $138,000 for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to the corresponding periods of 2025. The decreases were primarily attributable to capitalization of approximately $33,000 and $107,000 of interest expense during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, associated with debt incurred for construction projects, including our second PFAS reactor.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: We had no income tax expense for continuing operations for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025. Our effective tax rate was 0% for each period as a result of the full valuation allowance recognized against its U.S. federal and state deferred tax assets during the quarter ended September 30, 2024.

wc.text: Our expected cash requirements over the next twelve months include working capital needs, scheduled principal payments on debt, costs associated with the administration and monitoring of discontinued operations, R&D expenditures related to PFAS technology, and capital expenditures.

capex.text: Cash used in investing activities from continuing operations during the first nine months of 2026 consisted primarily of approximately $5,184,000 in purchases of property and equipment, $481,000 in advance payments for capital equipment and $381,000 in expenditures for operating permits and certain intangible assets, partially offset by $5,000 in proceeds from the sale of idle equipment.

net sales.heading: Revenues
net sales.text:
Consolidated revenues increased $494,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025, as follows:

(1) Includes waste generated by government clients of $685,000 and $560,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, and the corresponding period of 2025, respectively.

Treatment Segment revenue decreased by $1,513,000, or 11.5%, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared with the same period in 2025. The decline was primarily due to lower waste volume as discussed in the “Overview” section.

The increase in revenue in our Services Segment was primarily attributable to a higher volume of project work during the period compared with the same period in 2025. Revenue in our Services Segment is project-based and is influenced by the scope, duration, timing, and completion of individual projects.

Treatment.text: Despite these challenges, continued waste receipts, combined with delays in processing of certain waste streams, contributed to an increase in our Treatment Segment backlog to approximately $19,608,000 at September 30, 2026, representing an increase of approximately 24.6% from $15,733,000 at June 30, 2026. We believe this growing backlog supports future treatment activities; however, the timing of revenue recognized from our backlog may vary depending on waste complexity, customer requirements, and operational considerations.

Services.text: Our Services Segment revenue increased during the third quarter of 2026 compared with the corresponding period of 2025, primarily driven by increased project activity, including projects awarded since the beginning of 2026. These awards included a two-year master task agreement awarded in the first quarter of 2026 with an estimated value of approximately $24 million for demolition and disposal services at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (“LLNL”). However, revenue growth was partially constrained by customer-related delays in the mobilization of a project awarded during the early part of the second quarter of 2026. The project has since been mobilized.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: For 2025, the Treatment Segment accounted for $45,097,000, or 73.1%, of total revenue, as compared to $34,953,000, or 59.1%, of total revenue for 2024.
For 2025, the Services Segment accounted for $16,577,000, or 26.9% of total revenue, as compared to $24,164,000, or 40.9% of total revenue for 2024.

Our revenue derived from federal government entities, either directly as a prime contractor or indirectly for others as subcontractor to federal government entities, totaled $39,243,000, or 63.6% of total revenue in 2025, compared to $40,550,000, or 68.6% of total revenue in 2024.

The Company’s revenue derived from federal government entities, either directly as a prime contractor or indirectly for others as subcontractor to federal government entities, totaled $ 39,243,000 , or 63.6 % of total revenue in 2025, compared to $ 40,550,000 , or 68.6 % of total revenue in 2024.

The extent to which these regulatory trends translate into sustained commercial demand for PFAS destruction services will depend on a number of factors, including the pace and scope of federal and state implementation, the availability and acceptance of alternative disposal or treatment methods, customer adoption decisions, and our ability to secure regulatory approvals, contracts, and operational capacity to meet market needs.

Our ability to make scheduled principal and interest payments, refinance existing indebtedness, and borrow under our credit facility depends on our future operating performance and cash flows, which are subject to prevailing economic conditions and financial, competitive, business, and other factors, many of which are beyond our control.
Our ability to continue our operations depends on our ability to generate profitable operations or complete equity or debt financings to increase our capital, when needed.
Our ability to use the net loss carryforwards depends on whether we are able to generate sufficient income in the future years.
Our success depends on the contributions of our key management, environmental and engineering personnel.
Our future success depends on our ability to retain and expand our staff of qualified personnel, including environmental specialists and technicians, sales personnel, and engineers.
We also rely on the services of a variety of vendors to meet our data processing and communications needs.

Our program relies on a philosophy of continuous improvement by using periodic self-assessments, 3 rd party assessments, and customer/agency audits to determine cyber control presence, applicability, and effectiveness .

intro.text: Perma-Fix Environmental Services, Inc. is a nuclear services company and leading provider of nuclear and mixed waste management services. The Company’s nuclear waste services include management and treatment of radioactive and mixed waste for hospitals, research labs and institutions, federal agencies, including the DOE, U.S. Department of War (DOW), and the commercial nuclear industry. The Company’s nuclear services group provides project management, waste management, environmental restoration, decontamination and decommissioning, demolition, and radiological protection, safety and industrial hygiene capability to our clients. The Company operates four nuclear waste treatment facilities and provides nuclear services at DOE, DOW, and commercial facilities nationwide.
